correctness.rationale: The Newton expansion K_x=sum c_j T_j T_j^T has exact combinatorial coefficients; for j<k, c_j is bounded below by x^((k-j)^2)(2-exp(1/4)) on x<=1/(k-1). B_k=c_k decreases strictly there by an explicit derivative estimate, and is negative at the right endpoint. The Boolean-lattice up/down commutator proves T_{k-1} full column rank for n>=2k, giving endpoint rank, nullity and a strictly negative top-sector eigenvalue immediately outside the interval. An exact standalone Python checker passes 75 rational coefficient checks, 5300 entry identities, and 8410 direct top-sector components. The claim explicitly excludes the unclassified upper-x region.

originality.rationale: Krebs and Shaheen (2008) establish the generic Johnson adjacency spectra, not this all-k n-independent first Gaussian loss or boundary rank. Feragen et al. establish general Gaussian-kernel geometric obstructions, not this finite Johnson threshold. An earlier result for Hamming products uses the same top-difference polynomial B_k but has a different ambient metric and does not imply the sharp Johnson lower bound or endpoint rank. Checked public-index hits concern Johnson spectral concentration and Hamming shell problems without the claimed all-k frontier. Residual risk: an unlocated general positivity-cone theorem might yield the present result as an immediate specialization.
